small_guidance:
- The fused_lse kernel reloads x_conv from global memory for every group iteration even though it's the same tensor — restructure the loop to load each channel's x once, compute its normalized value using the per-group (mean, invstd) looked up by channel index, and accumulate into the online LSE state. This halves global memory traffic for the dominant kernel.
- Add larger BLOCK_S configs (e.g. 8192) and try num_warps=16; with S=15876 per (N), fewer blocks per row reduces per-program overhead and lets the conv epilogue dominate.
- Preload gamma/beta and mean/invstd for all C channels into registers at kernel start (C=64 is tiny) instead of issuing tl.load inside the channel loop — removes 64×2 scalar loads per program.
large_guidance:
- Conv2d (128×8×128×128 → 128×64×126×126, kernel 3×3) is the heaviest op and is still being run by cuDNN. Replace it with a custom Triton im2col-GEMM kernel using channels_last layout (BLOCK_M=64/128 over output spatial, BLOCK_N=64 over OC, BLOCK_K=IC*kh*kw=72), and fuse the entire GN+Tanh+HardSwish+residual+LSE epilogue into the conv kernel by writing one program per (N, output-spatial tile) that computes all 64 output channels in registers, then reduces along C to a single LSE value — eliminating the x_conv materialization (128×64×126×126 fp32 ≈ 500MB of read/write traffic).
- Alternatively, do a two-pass design where pass 1 = conv-GN-stats producing only mean/invstd (single program per (N,G) doing conv on the fly), pass 2 = conv-GN-activate-LSE producing the final output. This keeps the LSE pass register-resident across all 64 channels (4 channels per warp × 16 warps fits) and removes the intermediate x_conv tensor entirely.
- If keeping the current 3-kernel structure, at minimum fuse the groupnorm_stats pass with a single read of x_conv that also feeds the LSE pass via shared global writes — currently x_conv is read twice (stats + LSE), which is the main bandwidth tax.
